name: Data Analyzer: Rule extraction from PDF text stays fast on pathological text
objective: Proves crafted text cannot make the manual PDF rule search hang (a 'regex denial of service').
precondition: No file needed; synthetic strings only. Not an exact timing but a 3-second ceiling.

steps.action: Extract rules from each hostile text and time it
steps.data: 5 texts: 200,000 letters; 50,000 letters then 'range' then 50,000 digits; 40,000 repeats of 'word'; 30,000 repeats of 'x1' then 'between'; 200 lines of 5,000 letters
steps.expected: Each extraction finishes in under 3 seconds (the old patterns took minutes). The rules returned are not checked

name: Data Analyzer: Rule extraction still finds date fields and numeric ranges
objective: Proves the faster code still extracts the correct rules.

steps.action: Extract rules from three made-up lines
steps.data: 'birth_date is a date field', 'age valid range 18 to 85', 'notes free text'
steps.expected: birth_date is a date; age has minimum 18 and maximum 85; 'notes' gets no rule

name: Data Analyzer: A 'range' with only one number produces no rule
objective: Proves incomplete range text is ignored instead of producing a wrong rule.

name: Data Analyzer: Upload size limit defaults to 25 MB and can be changed
objective: Proves the limit in bytes follows the UI_MAX_UPLOAD_MB setting.

steps.action: Read the limit with no setting
Set UI_MAX_UPLOAD_MB to 10 and read again

name: Data Analyzer: A bad upload-limit setting falls back to 25 MB, never to unlimited
objective: Proves invalid values cannot remove the limit.

steps.action: Set UI_MAX_UPLOAD_MB to each bad value and read the limit
steps.expected: The limit is 25 MB each time

name: Data Analyzer: Page upload limit of 25 MB is below the API's 100 MB
objective: Intended to show the page limit is stricter than the service limit. In practice it only compares two fixed numbers written in the test.

steps.expected: 25 MB is less than 100 MB. This is always true: the test reads neither the page code nor the API setting

name: Data Analyzer: PDF with too many pages is refused with a clear message
objective: Proves the page-count limit is enforced and the message says how many pages and what the limit is.
precondition: A fake PDF reader with 6 pages ('x' each); limit 5 pages, 1000 characters.

steps.action: Extract text from the 6-page fake PDF
steps.expected: A 'too large' error whose message matches '6 pages; the limit is 5'

name: Data Analyzer: PDF with too much text is refused with a clear message
objective: Proves the character limit is enforced.
precondition: A fake PDF reader with 2 pages of 600 characters each; limit 5 pages, 1000 characters.

steps.expected: A 'too large' error whose message mentions 'characters'

name: Data Analyzer: PDF within the limits returns all of its text
precondition: A fake PDF reader with 2 pages ('one', 'two'); limits 5 pages, 1000 characters.

steps.expected: The result is exactly 'one', new line, 'two', new line

name: Data Analyzer: PDF page limit can be set by an environment variable
objective: Proves UI_PDF_MAX_PAGES is honoured when no limit is passed in.
precondition: A fake PDF reader with 3 pages; UI_PDF_MAX_PAGES=2.

steps.action: Extract text from the 3-page fake PDF

name: Data Analyzer: Non-PDF dictionary text has the same character limit
objective: Proves plain-text dictionaries are also size-limited, and text exactly at the limit is accepted.

steps.expected: The same text is returned unchanged
